title: Activator for the NGSadmix .qopt loader
_doc: Activate-schema for the loader at shared/loaders/qopt_loader.js. Describes the inputs needed to invoke the loader: paths to the headerless whitespace-separated .qopt and the sidecar samples.txt, plus producer params (at minimum K) for provenance. This is the FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE of the activate-schema pattern from the chat 39 cont. post-step22 design discussion. The pair (this activate-schema + ancestry_global_q_v1 extract-schema) is the template every future tool wiring should follow: one schema describing what the producer needs, one schema describing what it emits.

producer.name: load_ngsadmix_qopt
producer._doc: Reads .qopt + samples.txt and emits a self-describing ancestry_global_q_v1 artifact. Local-only: no HTTP across networks; the fetcher just wraps fetch() against the dev server serving the data folder. Sibling producer 'ancestry_groupwise_q' (in operations.registry.json) emits the SAME extract-schema via a server-side run on a sample subset — that's the conditional-ancestry path Quentin raised (post-step22). Both producers' artifacts are interchangeable downstream because they share the extract-schema.

qopt_path.description: Filesystem path to the headerless whitespace-separated .qopt file. NGSadmix's native output. Typically templated as 'data/cohort/ancestry/global/K{K}/ngsadmix.qopt' or similar. Absolute or relative-to-data-root, both fine; the dev server resolves it.

samples_path.description: Filesystem path to the sidecar samples.txt — one sample_id per line, blank/comment lines skipped. Must have exactly N entries where N matches the number of rows in the .qopt; the loader cross-checks and throws on mismatch. Convention: lives next to the .qopt in the same K{K} folder.

params.description: Producer params for provenance. K is required (the loader cross-checks against .qopt column count). Other fields are optional but encouraged — they're stuffed into produced_by.params on the emitted artifact, where they survive forever as metadata.

K.description: Number of ancestry components NGSadmix was run with. Cross-checked against the .qopt column count; mismatch throws.

run_id.description: Human-readable run identifier (e.g. 'broodstock_qc_pass_v1', 'natora_pruned_81_v1'). Optional but strongly encouraged — distinguishes parallel runs with the same K.

seed.description: Random seed NGSadmix was invoked with. Optional. Only knowable by reading the slurm log or the producer's invocation script.

snp_set.description: Identifier for the SNP set used (e.g. 'pruned_r2_0.1_LD500kb'). Optional but useful when comparing runs across different upstream filters.

samples_subset.description: Identifier for the sample subset used (e.g. 'all_226', 'natora_81', 'F12_only'). For genome-wide / per-chrom global runs this is typically the full cohort or NAToRA-pruned set. For conditional ancestry (band-1 vs band-2) this names the karyotype-derived subset.

scope.description: What scope this ancestry run covers. genome_wide: full genome aggregate; per_chrom: one chromosome only; per_band: a karyotype-band-conditional subset (typically calls the popgen_server, NOT this loader).

chrom.description: When scope=per_chrom, which chromosome (e.g. 'LG28'). Required if scope is per_chrom; ignored otherwise.

_examples._label: Genome-wide K=6 on the full 226-sample cohort

_sibling_producers.name: ancestry_groupwise_q
_sibling_producers._doc: Server-side run via popgen_server. Emits the SAME extract-schema (ancestry_global_q_v1) but takes a sample-subset artifact and a beagle path as inputs, runs NGSadmix on the cluster, returns the result. Used for conditional-ancestry (band-1 vs band-2) where the .qopt does not exist on disk yet.

_design_provenance: First-class activate-schema; created during chat 39 cont. (round 5 step 22+) as the worked example of the 'each tool gets one extract-schema and at minimum one activate-schema' rule (Quentin's design directive 2026-05-07). All future tool wirings (.res / ngsRelate, .beagle.gz, KING, pyrho, ...) follow this template.
